name: Butterfly haircut

lead: The butterfly haircut is a long, layered style in which shorter face-framing layers sit over longer lengths, producing a lifted, voluminous shape. It was popularised around 2022 on social media and by celebrities.

For looks, layers around the face can draw attention to cheekbones and eyes and make fine hair look fuller. Styling usually involves blow-drying for lift, with the short layers directed away from the face.

paras: It is requested from a hairdresser as layers cut around the face and through the length, often with reference photos and a note on where the short layers should start. Day to day it is blow-dried with a round brush or curled, and trims every six to eight weeks keep the shape.
There are few risks beyond those of any haircut: heat styling can dry hair, layers need trims to hold shape, and one stylist guide notes layers can make very thin hair look thinner.

chain: Short layers cut around the face
angle.text: The cut changes the outline of the hair around the face and adds body. Layers starting at the cheekbones suit round faces, while softer layers from the chin suit angular faces, according to L'Oreal.[1] The effect shows immediately after styling.

lead: The butterfly haircut is a layered style that pairs short, face-framing layers with longer layers through the rest of the hair, so the hair gains volume at the crown and around the face while keeping its length.[1] Stylists compare the lifted, outward-flicked layers to butterfly wings, and PureWow quotes the stylist who named it describing it as two haircuts in one.[2]

People choose it to add body and movement, to soften the outline around the face, and to make fine hair look fuller; L'Oreal says it can add lift to fine straight hair, remove bulk from thick hair and help curls spring up.[1] The short layers are usually placed at the cheekbones or chin depending on face shape.[1][3]
The cut was popularised around 2022, with the name credited to celebrity stylist Sunnie Brook, and it draws on 1970s layered looks.[2][4] No published studies have examined it.
infobox: Shoulder-length or longer; short bob versions exist[1][2]
Short face-framing layers over long layers[1]

paras: The style is built from layers of different lengths so the hair holds volume and curves outward near the face. PureWow describes the short layers as sitting about two to three inches below the chin, with longer layers falling past the shoulders.[2] John Frieda notes it is sometimes called the octopus haircut and that its transitions are softer and more polished than a wolf cut.[3]

Variations include a short butterfly bob for fine hair, a long version that separates the below-chin layers, a curly version that enhances natural volume, and a colour-treated version in which colour highlights the layers.[2]

L'Oreal says the cut works on straight, wavy and curly hair, and John Frieda says it suits fine hair because layering gives the look of fullness.[1][3] A Glam piece advises that thicker hair carries it best and that layers can make thin hair look thinner, suggesting a stylist adjust the cut to the person.[4] Fringe choices such as curtain bangs or a side-swept fringe are matched to face shape.[1][3]

Typical styling is a blow-dry with a round brush to lift the crown and direct the short layers away from the face; curling irons, rollers and heatless methods are alternatives, and curly hair can be scrunched with a leave-in product and air-dried or diffused.[1][3] Texturising spray or leave-in conditioner can add definition.[2]

Trims are suggested every six to eight weeks, or every 10 to 12 weeks while growing it out.[1][3] Stylists advise bringing reference photos to the salon and stating texture, length and upkeep preferences.[2][4]

L'Oreal traces the modern version to the 1970s, when airy layered cuts first became mainstream.[1] PureWow says the butterfly cut appeared in 2022, named by stylist Sunnie Brook, and links it to celebrities including Hailee Steinfeld, Sydney Sweeney, Jennifer Lopez and Zendaya, who wore a butterfly bob.[2] Glam describes it as drawing on retro 1970s and 1990s styles.[4]

timeline.event: Airy layered cuts become mainstream, a forerunner of the butterfly cut.[1]
The butterfly cut is named by stylist Sunnie Brook and spreads among celebrities and social media.[2]
